title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 19–21). Grothendieck is axiomatizing 1-dimensional 'forms' (on p. 21 these become 'réseaux', i.e. networks) without using point-set topology. The data are a set of places (lieux) L and a family S of subsets of L called segments. Each segment I has a boundary ∂I consisting of two points, an interior I° = I \ ∂I, and is linearly ordered between its endpoints. For x, y in I, I_{x,y} denotes the sub-segment of I between x and y. The page fixes the axiom F6 and spells out its consequences.

The notion of branch. Take two segments I, J with a common endpoint x. They 'define the same branchement at x' if they share an initial piece: there is y ≠ x in I° ∩ J° with I_{x,y} = J_{x,y}. This is exactly the notion of a germ of arc at x, or a 'direction' at x as in R-tree theory.

Axiom F6. If I and J have the same branch at x, then there is K in S with x ∈ ∂K and I° ∪ J° ⊂ K°. Reformulated: for a fixed point x and a fixed branch at x, the set of interiors I° of segments issuing from x along that branch is filtered increasing (directed) for inclusion. Since K is linearly ordered from x, this forces I and J to be nested. So the union of segments along a branch is a single 'ray'.

The axiom only makes sense if segments cannot pass through a branching point in their interior. In a Y-shaped graph the arcs [x,a] and [x,b] share a germ at x but lie in no common segment. This reading fits p. 21:
- a node is a place of multiplicity ≠ 2;
- a network is 'réduit' when every segment has empty interior, i.e. segments are just edges between nodes.

The proposition after F6 ('comparison with F7', apparently an older numbering). Let x ∈ ∂I ∩ ∂J.
- (a) Same branch at x ⇔ there is K ∈ S with x ∈ ∂K and I ∪ J ⊂ K. The implication ⇐ is immediate: I and J are initial pieces of K from x, so take y near x. The implication ⇒ comes from F6.
- (b) Otherwise the germs are disjoint: there are u ∈ I°, v ∈ J° with I_{x,u} ∩ J_{x,v} = {x}.

So two arcs from a point either share a germ or have disjoint germs. This dichotomy is what lets one define the set of branches at x, and hence the multiplicity of a place, used on p. 21.

Marginal NB, partly illegible. It seems to say that F6 does not require any statement about I ∩ J, because such a statement follows from the property of K (cf. F7).

Purpose. These are the local-structure axioms that make a 'form' a possibly non-locally-finite graph with real-like edges. The result is a combinatorial-ordered model of 1-dimensional tame spaces.
errors: F6 as stated is false if segments may pass through branch points (Y-graph counterexample). It is consistent only if segments are tacitly arcs without interior nodes, which p. 21 suggests but which is not stated as an axiom on this page.

Passing from F6's conclusion (I° ∪ J° ⊂ K°) to (a)'s 'I ∪ J ⊂ K' needs the far endpoints of I and J to lie in K. This requires an extra closure/extension argument or another axiom; it is not justified on the page.
In (b), 'I_{x,u} ∩ I_{x,v}' is evidently a slip for I_{x,u} ∩ J_{x,v}.

(b) presumably also uses an axiom not on this page, guaranteeing that the intersection of two segments with a common endpoint is a common initial segment or reduces to {x} near x. The margin NB seems to concern exactly this point.

ideas.what: Branch/germ at a point x defined as equivalence of segments issuing from x that share an initial sub-segment.
ideas.modern_name: directions (germs of arcs) at a point, as in R-trees / tangent space of directions in metric graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; formalized in R-tree theory (Morgan–Shalen, Chiswell, 1980s) and in Berkovich-space/metric-graph literature

ideas.what: Axiom F6: segments with a common germ at x are nested (the family of their interiors is directed), i.e. no branching inside segments.
ideas.modern_name: axiomatics of 1-dimensional spaces via segment/betweenness systems (pretrees, interval structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: betweenness/pretree axiomatics (Ward, Bowditch 'treelike structures' 1999; van de Vel convex structures)

ideas.what: Dichotomy: two segments from x either share a germ or have germs meeting only in x; prepares the definition of the multiplicity of a place (2 at regular places, nodes otherwise).
ideas.modern_name: valence/degree of a point in a topological graph or dendrite (number of branches)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical continuum theory (Menger–Urysohn order of a point)

ideas.what: Overall program: a 'géométrie des formes' axiomatizing tame 1-dimensional shapes combinatorially (place sets with ordered segments) instead of via topology.
ideas.modern_name: tame topology / combinatorial models of 1-dimensional spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's tame-topology vision (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); o-minimality (van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses 'topologie modérée' in general terms but not this axiomatics

missed.claim: Part of an unpublished 1986 attempt to axiomatize 1-dimensional 'forms'/networks by ordered segment systems: a concrete, if elementary, piece of Grothendieck's tame-topology program that is not reflected in the literature. The page contains only routine local lemmas.
missed.quote: l'ensemble des I°, I ∈ S tels que x ∈ ∂I, et que I ait un branchement donné, [est] filtrant croissant pour l'inclusion
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for reconstructing how Grothendieck intended to realize 'topologie modérée' after the Esquisse. Mathematically it overlaps known pretree/R-tree/betweenness axiomatics.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is elementary local axiomatics of graph-like spaces (germs of arcs, the shared-germ-or-disjoint dichotomy), well known in equivalent forms. The only interest is historical: an unpublished 1986 concrete step in the 'géométrie des formes' / tame-topology program.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 should read 'définissent le même branchement'; the added '{+y ≠ x+}' belongs to '∃ y ∈ I° ∩ J°, y ≠ x'.
'[?] filtrant croissant' is likely '[est] filtrant croissant'.
In (b), the image (and logic) suggest I_{x,u} ∩ J_{x,v} = {x}; the transcribed 'I_{x,u} ∩ I_{x,v}' reproduces a slip.
Page number at top is 20 (overwritten), archive folio 22.
The first line's '{+x ∈ L+}' is an interlinear insertion above 'tels que'.
